item.title: Corps news roundup: new directors, brass staffs, and audition season
item.description:
DCI's latest corps news roundup covers the offseason moves shaping the 2027 season. The Boston Crusaders named a new corps director, while the Raiders, Cavaliers, and Music City all introduced new brass staffs — key hires that will shape each corps' sound and show design next summer.

The roundup also takes readers inside one of Pacific Crest's first audition camps as corps begin building their 2027 rosters, plus updates from the DCI All-Age and SoundSport circuits. With audition season underway, the offseason is officially in full swing.

item.title: Phantom Regiment to Tour California for the First Time in 10 Years
item.description:
Phantom Regiment has a roadmap in place to tour the West Coast for the first time in a decade as part of the 2027 Drum Corps International Tour. The corps announced plans for its first California tour since 2016, bringing its show to West Coast audiences who have only been able to follow the corps from afar for years.

For West Coast drum corps fans, it's a rare chance to see one of DCI's most storied corps live, and for Phantom Regiment it's a significant logistical undertaking — cross-country touring is expensive and demanding, which is why so few eastern and midwestern corps make the trip. The announcement is an early signal that the 2027 tour is shaping up to be an expansive one.

item.title: Latin American Ensembles Eye the DCI Tour as Global Momentum Grows
item.description:
Representatives from prominent drum corps and marching bands across Central America gathered virtually on October 29 for a strategic discussion about opportunities on the DCI Tour, a sign of expanding international enthusiasm for the marching arts. The meeting reflects growing interest from Latin American ensembles in participating in Drum Corps International's competitive circuit.

DCI has been steadily internationalizing — corps from Asia and Europe have already made the trip — and Latin American participation would widen the activity's footprint further. For the ensembles involved, touring with DCI offers exposure to the highest level of the marching arts; for DCI, it's another step toward a genuinely global competitive field rather than a largely North American one.

item.title: Joe Marrella, who pioneered the eight-person snare drum line, dies at 83
item.description:
Joe Marrella, a 1995 DCI Hall of Fame inductee known for his larger-than-life personality, died October 30 in New Jersey at the age of 83. Marrella pioneered the eight-person snare drum line, a formation that reshaped how drum corps thought about the battery — bigger, louder, and more visually commanding than what had come before.

His influence runs through decades of drum corps percussion. The eight-person snare line became a standard of the activity's modern sound, and Marrella's showmanship left its mark on the culture of DCI as well. He is remembered as both an innovator and a character.
